justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I assessed as the prevailing price level around 1,220–1,225, with each horizon nudging slightly higher to account for a gentle underlying trend. For the one-day estimate, I anchored closely to recent trading levels, assuming no major news breaks and that intraday momentum carries forward marginally. For the one-week estimate, I incorporated a small positive drift consistent with whatever medium-term trend was in place, while acknowledging that a week is long enough for meaningful mean-reversion or continuation depending on macro signals. The one-month estimate extends that drift further but remains conservative, as a month is long enough for the fundamental backdrop to shift materially, yet short enough that I didn't want to project aggressive directional moves without stronger conviction.

The confidence interval widths widen predictably as the horizon extends, reflecting the square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty that governs most financial price processes. At one day, the range is relatively tight because intraday volatility, while real, is bounded by the limited time available for news and sentiment to accumulate. By one week, I've widened the interval to capture the realistic possibility of a meaningful macro release, central bank commentary, or geopolitical development shifting the price by three to five percent in either direction. At one month, the interval is wide enough to encompass a genuine trend reversal, as the cumulative effect of compounding daily uncertainties makes the tails quite fat.

The specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals fall into a few categories. A sudden and unexpected policy shift from a major central bank, particularly around interest rates or quantitative tightening, could move prices sharply beyond the monthly bounds. A geopolitical shock, such as an escalation in an ongoing conflict or a new flashpoint, could drive safe-haven or risk-off flows that blow past my one-day interval in a single session. On the downside, an unexpectedly strong economic data release signaling robust growth and reduced recession risk could cause a sharp reversal that breaks below my lower bounds. Liquidity events, such as a major fund liquidation or a flash crash driven by algorithmic activity, represent tail risks that are by definition difficult to model and could temporarily push prices well outside any reasonable interval I might construct.
